svg.text: Chromium: Decode Now, Vulkan Encode Next
Plan-first: the NVIDIA VA-API bridge port closes today's decode gap while the Vulkan-native backends mature — upstream pushes begin end of July 2026.
DELIVERED
Track 1 — VA-API decode port for NVIDIA (the temporary bridge)
Chromium's existing VA-API backend already served Intel and AMD GPUs with their codecs — NVIDIA was the gap. NVIDIA
delivered a VA-API port to fill it temporarily: users get HW-accelerated decode today, with zero new API plumbing.
A bridge to the future Vulkan Video work: decode is accelerated now; Vulkan replaces it underneath, for every vendor.
IN DEVELOPMENT
Track 2 — Vulkan Video decoder
Per-codec accelerator delegates (H.264/H.265/AV1/VP9) converting Chromium's parsed headers into Vulkan Std structures;
DMA-buf export with DRM format modifiers for zero-copy VideoFrames into the compositor (gfx::NativePixmapDmaBuf).
Replaces per-platform VA-API/V4L2/DXVA with one cross-vendor backend.
UPSTREAMING
Track 3 — Vulkan Video encoder (the strategic decision)
Built on the Vulkan Video Samples library, vendored and statically linked into Chromium (the libvpx/libaom pattern) and driven
through a codec-neutral VideoEncodeAccelerator backend on the compositor's own VkDevice. Working H.264 encode with the
SharedImage zero-copy input path verified on NVIDIA hardware (bit-identical to the staging reference, PSNR-gated in CI);
lights up WebRTC, WebCodecs, MediaRecorder, and Cast through the one GPU-process encoder factory.
⭢ Upstream CLs to chromium.org begin end of July 2026
How the work is shared
NVIDIA — the port itself: backends, library, drivers, conformance · AMD & Intel — HW acceleration bring-up and validation on their GPUs (Mesa RADV/ANV)
Google — Chromium change reviews and browser-framework improvements (notably GPU zero-copy plumbing) · Khronos Vulkan Video TSG — API stewardship & CTS
